panels.title: Audience & scale
panels.description: Aggregate audience activity and service scale. These are context metrics, not fault thresholds.

panels.title: Capacity
panels.description: Current and projected D1 and Durable Objects rows written are separate UTC-day resources. Values come from delayed, approximate Cloudflare analytics; cyan is comfortable, amber and coral indicate capacity risk.

panels.title: Service traffic · 24h
panels.description: Aggregate Worker requests in finalized five-minute windows. Disconnected clients are context rather than service failure.

panels.title: Database activity · 24h
panels.description: D1 rows read and written in delayed, finalized five-minute Cloudflare analytics windows.

panels.title: Notifications Sent
panels.description: FCM outcomes between settled five-minute UTC collector samples. Collection runs at :30 after each boundary and normally attributes one aligned scheduler tick per interval; precise-live sends can occur between ticks. Blue means Firebase accepted the send; it does not confirm handset delivery. Coral shows failed attempts. Values are exact deltas from persisted counters; a failed collector sample is recovered by the next successful sample without loss or double counting.

visualEditor.code: return { dataset: context.editor.dataset, series: context.editor.series, xAxis: { type: 'time' }, yAxis: { type: 'value' } };

panels.title: Invalid tokens · 24h
panels.description: Audience & scale — unique FCM token lifecycles that returned a permanent invalid-token response and entered automatic cleanup in the rolling last 24 hours. This can indicate an uninstall or token rotation, but is not proof of an uninstall and is normal lifecycle evidence rather than a service fault.

visualEditor.code: return { dataset: context.editor.dataset, series: context.editor.series, xAxis: { type: 'time' }, yAxis: { type: 'value' } };
